identity.fantasy: A dual-two-handed demonic fortress that converts avoidance into armor and resistance, then leeches through incoming pressure.
identity.one_line: A dual-two-handed demonic fortress that converts avoidance into armor and resistance, then leeches through incoming pressure. The defining decision is contextual: Incoming pressure determines whether Carve can safely be exchanged for Fireball.

mechanics.core_loop: A dual-two-handed demonic tank that converts avoidance into armor and magic resistance, uses Carve and retaliation for threat, and leeches or heals through aggression. Its defining cooldowns include Tyrannical Resolve and group mitigation through Infernal Whipcrack. Recent players describe extremely high durability, though that does not prove comparative balance.
mechanics.single_target: Maintain barrier and Inner Demon uptime, use Twin Slice for single-target pressure, and never cast Smite without Inner Demon. The captured guide trades Carve for Fireball only when survivability permits.
mechanics.aoe: Felrend, Sunder, Sargeron, Carve, and retaliation form the pack engine. The guide treats Carve-to-Fireball as an explicit survival-for-damage trade rather than a free upgrade.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Hybrid demonic tools aid contact, but its core durability comes from active melee aggression.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Its structural defensive package includes Burning Commander, Demonic Will, Nether Disciple, Demon Hide, Pure Hatred.
mechanics.group_utility: Group or control tools include Betrayer, Felblade, Eye of the Tyrant.

failure_modes.text: Casting Smite outside Inner Demon, replacing Carve when defense is still needed, or overlapping barrier and mitigation windows can expose the tank suddenly.
Casting Smite without Inner Demon violates the guide's central damage and survival rule.
